purpose: Integrates WP 6.7+ native WebP/AVIF support, adds native lazy loading toggle with browser-level loading="lazy" attribute, JSON schema for 16 REST endpoints, cache group flushing via wp_cache_flush_group(), modern WP 6.7+ defer strategy using wp_script_add_data, and WP 6.9+ wp_cache_add_salt() support to Redis object cache.
riskRationale: Contains two critical regressions: (1) AVIF conversion hooks are silently skipped when WP 6.7+ is detected and the user selects 'both' or 'avif' format, and (2) delay JS is completely non-functional on all supported WordPress versions because the script_loader_tag filter that handled it is no longer registered. Additionally, excluded images lose forced fetchpriority/decoding on WP 6.3+.
breakingChanges: Excluded images (via exclusion list) no longer receive forced fetchpriority='high' and decoding='sync' on WP 6.3+ due to incomplete fallback handling in set_loading_optimization_attributes()

Delay JS (file_optimisation.delayJS) is silently broken on all supported WP versions because the script_loader_tag filter for add_defer_attribute is only registered when wp_script_add_data doesn't exist (never on WP 6.2+)

text: The PR correctly adds modern WP feature detection and introduces useful new capabilities across image optimization, caching, REST API, and script loading. However, it contains two critical regressions: AVIF conversion is silently skipped for 'both'/'avif' users on WP 6.7+, and delay JS is non-functional on all supported versions. Three previously reported issues have been fixed correctly. The native lazy loading feature and cache salt integration are well-implemented and backward-compatible.

reasoning: Two critical bugs block merge: (1) AVIF conversion hooks are skipped on WP 6.7+ when format is 'avif' or 'both', and (2) delay JS is broken because the script_loader_tag filter was made conditional on a function that always exists. Both have straightforward, safe fixes under 5 lines each.

message: The core_handles_webp() check via wp_image_quality function_exists is a clean, version-agnostic detection mechanism.
Extracting loading optimization into a dedicated set_loading_optimization_attributes() method is good separation of concerns.
The flush_group() method is a useful addition with proper function_exists guard for backward compatibility.
The add_defer_strategy method correctly uses wp_script_add_data with 'strategy' => 'defer' for WP 6.7+, which is cleaner than regex-based defer injection.
Adding JSON schema to all 16 REST routes improves API discoverability and integration with WP REST API tooling.
The $needs_script optimization cleanly skips enqueuing lazyload JS when native lazy loading handles images and no videos/delayed JS are needed.
The useNativeLazy detection and dynamic LAZY_SELECTOR that narrows to only videos in native mode is clean and efficient.
Cache salt integration in get_key() between prefix and group with empty-string default is fully backward-compatible.
Both WP_HTML_Tag_Processor and regex fallback paths handle lazyLoadNative consistently, avoiding duplicate attributes.

The hook condition `! (core_handles_webp() && 'avif' === get_format())` incorrectly skips the wp_generate_attachment_metadata filter when format is 'avif' (either selected directly or after downgrade from 'both'). This silently prevents AVIF conversion from triggering on attachment upload on WP 6.7+. Conversion only happens lazily on first visitor request via maybe_serve_next_gen_image, meaning uploaded images are never pre-converted to AVIF.
suggestion: Replace the condition to skip the hook only when format is 'none' (the downgraded value when core handles WebP), allowing the hook for 'avif' and original formats.

message: Delay JS is completely broken because the script_loader_tag filter for add_defer_attribute is only registered when wp_script_add_data doesn't exist. Since wp_script_add_data has existed since WP 5.7 and the plugin requires WP 6.2+, the else branch never executes. The add_defer_attribute method handles both defer AND delay JS (wppo-src attribute swapping), so delay JS is silently non-functional on all supported versions. Additionally, the function_exists guard is dead code.
suggestion: Always register the script_loader_tag filter for delay JS independently of the defer strategy. The defer handling can use wp_script_add_data for WP 6.7+, but delay JS still needs the script_loader_tag filter. Extract delay JS into its own always-registered filter while using add_defer_strategy for defer only.

message: set_loading_optimization_attributes() completely ignores the $defaults fallback when wp_get_loading_optimization_attributes() is available (WP 6.3+). Excluded images (which should receive forced fetchpriority='high' and decoding='sync') instead get whatever WordPress decides, which may be empty. This is a behavior regression for all WP 6.3+ installs using the exclusion feature.
suggestion: Apply fallback defaults after the core function result, overriding any empty/missing values to ensure the plugin's exclusion list is respected while still using core's optimization hints.

message: fetchpriority='low' is passed as an argument to wp_enqueue_script for script tags. fetchpriority is NOT a valid attribute for <script> elements in the HTML spec — it only applies to images, iframes, and link elements. This attribute will be ignored by browsers, making it dead code.
suggestion: Remove fetchpriority from script args since it has no effect on <script> elements. If the intent was to deprioritize this script, use 'strategy' => 'defer' or load it in the footer with later priority instead.

message: The convert_image() skip guard checks `'webp' === $format` but not `'both'`. If called externally with 'both' on WP 6.7+, the guard is bypassed and the method attempts both WebP and AVIF conversion. The WebP attempt would overlap with core's native generation.
suggestion: Add a 'both' check to the guard, or handle it by stripping 'webp' from the format list when core_handles_webp().

message: When native lazy is active and the JS script is still loaded (because videos or delay JS are needed), loadImages() creates IntersectionObserver and MutationObserver instances that manage only video elements. If no videos are present, checkCleanup() disconnects them immediately, but the initial setup overhead and MutationObserver on document.body with subtree:true still occurs briefly.
suggestion: Early-return from loadImages() when useNativeLazy is true and no video elements match LAZY_SELECTOR, avoiding unnecessary observer creation.
